page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-8GB is a virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features two shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 40 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core performance is more constrained, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average and weak categories respectively. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently register in the average tier, while Passmark memory and database operations benchmarks are classified as weak.

The shared CPU allocation presents a clear tradeoff, as resource contention may limit sustained multi-threaded performance, as evidenced by weak multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench compiling scores. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point with strong single-threaded capabilities for lightweight workloads. It is suitable for basic web serving, text processing, and small-scale development tasks, but is not designed for resource-intensive database operations or multi-threaded processing.
